children: NIKE (NKE) reports fiscal Q1 after close. Analysts expect revenue ~$11.33–11.35B and EPS $0.44. Company has a history of recent revenue and earnings beats.
Short interest in NIKE, Inc. Class B (NKE) hit about 87 million shares, just over 7% of float; shorts rose roughly 55 million shares in the past 52 weeks.
NKE shares down ~44% YTD and >50% over 12 months, trading at multi‑year lows as analysts question the pace and effectiveness of Nike’s turnaround efforts.
Before NIKE (NKE) earnings, Oct 9 options show a 1.16 put/call ratio and implied move down ~7.7% to $32.91; shares trade below major moving averages with RSI around mid-30s.
Traders await NIKE (NKE) results, focusing on inventory, new product launches, regional sales (North America, Asia Pacific, Latin America) and Nike Direct trends after prior quarter decline.
NIKE Class B (NKE) forecasts Greater China revenue down ~13% to ~$1.3B, citing discounting, aging assortments and competition from Anta and Li Ning.
Analysts cut NIKE (NKE) price targets: RBC $40, Deutsche Bank $37, Piper Sandler $38, Evercore $34, BofA $30 (downgrade), Oppenheimer $52, Barclays $48; overall lower targets, mixed ratings.
NKE: Nike Direct revenue is seen down about 7% year-over-year; digital sales projected to drop roughly 12%, indicating direct-to-consumer gains didn’t boost overall demand during the period.
NKE refocuses on sport performance, reengages wholesale partners and curbs promotional discounting on lifestyle lines like Hoops Classics and Jordan streetwear; warns of potential short-term pain
NIKE Class B (NKE) may lose Kylian Mbappé as an endorsement. Management won’t address the exit in prepared remarks; analysts may ask about other contracted athletes during Q&A.
